results.structuredChinese: 我挺喜欢喝咖啡的，主要是因为早上经常比较困，喝一杯会让我清醒一点。现在这已经成了我的日常习惯，不过我通常一天只喝一杯。
results.spokenEnglish: I quite like coffee, mainly because I often feel pretty tired in the morning, and a cup helps me wake up a bit. It's become a daily habit now, though I usually stick to just one cup a day.

results.structuredChinese: 我挺喜欢喝咖啡的，主要是因为早上经常比较困，喝一杯会让我清醒一点。现在这已经成了我的日常习惯，不过我通常一天只喝一杯。
results.spokenEnglish: Yeah, I'm quite into coffee, mostly because I tend to feel pretty groggy in the mornings, so a cup really helps me wake up a bit. It's pretty much a daily habit for me now, though I usually stick to just one cup a day.

results.structuredChinese: 我挺喜欢喝咖啡的，主要是因为早上经常比较困，喝一杯会让我清醒一点。现在这已经成了我的日常习惯，不过我通常一天只喝一杯。
results.spokenEnglish: I do enjoy coffee, mostly because I'm usually pretty groggy in the morning, and a cup helps me wake up a bit. It's become part of my daily routine now, though I generally stick to just one cup a day.

results.structuredChinese: 周末我基本就是宅在家里，累了一周真的不想折腾。大部分时间就刷刷剧，算是给自己彻底放空一下，感觉这样最舒服。
results.spokenEnglish: I mostly just stay in on weekends, to be honest. After a tiring week, I really can't be bothered going out. I spend most of my time binge-watching shows — it's my way of completely switching off, and honestly, that's when I feel most relaxed.

results.structuredChinese: 我更喜欢住在大城市，主要是因为生活方便，工作机会也多。不过人确实太多了，有时候会觉得有点吵，尤其是上下班高峰期。
results.spokenEnglish: I definitely prefer living in a big city — mainly because everything's so convenient and there are way more job opportunities. That said, it can get pretty overwhelming with the crowds, and it does get noisy sometimes, especially during rush hour.

results.structuredChinese: 我以前不太喜欢看书，现在偶尔会看一点。主要看当时有没有时间和心情，不会强迫自己每天都读。
results.spokenEnglish: I didn't use to enjoy reading much, but I pick up a book every now and then these days. It really depends on whether I've got the time and I'm in the right mood — I don't force myself to read every day or anything.

results.structuredChinese: 我想说家里找到的一台旧相机。它不贵，外表也很普通，但拍出来的颜色偏暖，跟手机照片很不一样。带它出门有点麻烦，拍完也不能马上看到效果，不过我还是很喜欢。它会让我拍照时慢下来，更认真地观察眼前的东西，所以对我来说挺特别的。
results.spokenEnglish: I'd like to talk about an old camera I found at home. It wasn't expensive, and it looks pretty ordinary from the outside, but the photos come out with this warm colour tone that's really different from phone pictures. Taking it out is a bit of a hassle, and you can't check the results straight away, but I still really like it. It slows me down when I'm taking photos and makes me look more carefully at what's in front of me, so it feels quite special to me.

results.structuredChinese: 我想说家里找到的一台旧相机。它不贵，外表也很普通，但拍出来的颜色偏暖，跟手机照片很不一样。带它出门有点麻烦，拍完也不能马上看到效果，不过我还是很喜欢。它会让我拍照时慢下来，更认真地观察眼前的东西，所以对我来说挺特别的。
results.spokenEnglish: I'd like to talk about an old camera I found at home. It wasn't expensive, and it looks pretty ordinary on the outside, but the colours come out warm and slightly faded — nothing like the sharp, saturated photos you get from a phone. Taking it out is a bit of a hassle, and you can't check the shot straight away, which takes some getting used to. But I still love using it. It forces me to slow down and actually look at what's in front of me instead of just snapping away. That makes it special to me — it's more about the process than the result.

results.structuredChinese: 我想说家里找到的一台旧相机。它不贵，外表也很普通，但拍出来的颜色偏暖，跟手机照片很不一样。带它出门有点麻烦，拍完也不能马上看到效果，不过我还是很喜欢。它会让我拍照时慢下来，更认真地观察眼前的东西，所以对我来说挺特别的。
results.spokenEnglish: I'd like to talk about this old camera I found at home. It wasn't expensive, and honestly it looks pretty ordinary, but the colours come out warm — nothing like what you get on a phone. It's a bit of a hassle carrying it around, and you can't check the shot straight away, which takes some getting used to. But I still love it. What it does is force you to slow down, to actually look at what's in front of you rather than just snapping away. That's what makes it special to me.

results.structuredChinese: 去年夏天，我跟几个好朋友去了一趟海边，那是我第一次看到海上日出。第二天我们很早起床，天还黑着就走到海边。看到太阳从海平面慢慢升起来时，我觉得早起很值得。回来的路上大家都很累，但那次经历让我明白，有时候稍微折腾一下，能换来很特别的体验。
results.spokenEnglish: Last summer, I went to the seaside with a few close friends, and it was actually my first time seeing the sunrise over the ocean. We got up really early the next morning — it was still pitch black when we made our way down to the beach. Watching the sun slowly come up from the horizon, I just felt that getting up so early had been completely worth it. On the way back, everyone was pretty exhausted, but that whole experience made me realise that sometimes going a bit out of your way, putting in a little extra effort, can lead to something really memorable.

results.structuredChinese: 我想说一条旧围巾。那是几年前我刚工作时，我妈妈亲手织给我的。围巾是深灰色的，针脚不算整齐，但很厚实。后来每年冬天我都会拿出来戴，虽然边角已经起球了，我还是舍不得扔。它对我来说不只是一条围巾，更像是一种被家人惦记的感觉。
results.spokenEnglish: I'd like to talk about an old scarf my mum knitted for me when I'd just started working a few years back. It's a dark grey colour, and you can tell the stitches aren't exactly even — she's not a professional or anything — but it's incredibly thick and warm. Ever since then, I've pulled it out every winter without fail. The edges have gone all bobbly now, and it definitely looks worn, but I just can't bring myself to throw it away. To me, it's never really been just a scarf. It feels more like this tangible reminder that someone in my family is thinking of me, looking out for me in a way. That's what makes it irreplaceable, really.

results.structuredChinese: 我想说一位帮助过我的老师。以前我上课不太敢提问，总担心自己的问题太简单。她很耐心，从来不会因为学生答错而不耐烦，还会鼓励我慢慢说。后来我开始愿意举手，也更有信心了。我最感谢她的地方，是她让我觉得犯错并不可怕。
results.spokenEnglish: I'd like to talk about a teacher who really helped me out. I used to be quite hesitant about asking questions in class — I was always worried mine would sound too simple or even silly. But she was incredibly patient. She never got frustrated when a student gave the wrong answer, and she'd actually encourage me to take my time and just speak at my own pace. Gradually, I started putting my hand up more often, and I could feel my confidence growing bit by bit. What I'm most grateful for, though, is that she made me feel that making mistakes wasn't something to be afraid of — and that, looking back, has made a real difference to how I approach learning in general.

results.structuredChinese: 我觉得政府应该发展公共交通，因为城市堵车很严重。如果公交和地铁更方便，更多人会愿意少开车，这能减少拥堵和空气污染。不过不同城市情况不同，政府还是要根据当地需求选择合适的方式。
results.spokenEnglish: I think the government should develop public transport because traffic jams in cities are really serious. If buses and subways were more convenient, more people would be willing to drive less, and that would reduce both congestion and air pollution. But different cities have different situations, so the government still needs to choose suitable ways based on local needs.

results.structuredChinese: 我觉得政府应该发展公共交通，因为城市堵车很严重。如果公交和地铁更方便，更多人会愿意少开车，这能减少拥堵和空气污染。不过不同城市情况不同，政府还是要根据当地需求选择合适的方式。
results.spokenEnglish: I'd say investing in public transport is something the government should definitely prioritise, mainly because traffic congestion in cities has become such a serious problem. If buses and the underground were more convenient and reliable, I reckon a lot more people would be willing to leave their cars at home, and that would obviously ease congestion and cut down on air pollution too. At the same time, it really does depend on the city — what works in one place might not suit another — so the government still needs to tailor its approach to local needs rather than just applying the same solution everywhere.

results.structuredChinese: 我觉得政府应该发展公共交通，因为城市堵车很严重。如果公交和地铁更方便，更多人会愿意少开车，这能减少拥堵和空气污染。不过不同城市情况不同，政府还是要根据当地需求选择合适的方式。
results.spokenEnglish: I'd say investing in public transport is the way to go, simply because traffic congestion in cities has become such a headache. If buses and subways were genuinely convenient, more people would happily leave their cars at home, which would ease congestion and cut air pollution at the same time. That said, there's no one-size-fits-all solution — each city has its own set of challenges, so local governments still need to tailor their approach to what actually works on the ground.

results.structuredChinese: 我觉得远程工作确实方便，不用每天通勤，时间也更自由。但沟通会比较麻烦，比如线上等回复可能很久，有些复杂的事情只靠文字或视频也容易产生误解。所以它有明显好处，但公司需要找到改善沟通的方法。
results.spokenEnglish: Remote working is definitely convenient — you don't have to commute every day and you've got more flexibility with your time. But communication can be tricky. You might be waiting ages for a reply online, and with complicated issues, it's easy for things to get misunderstood when you're only using messages or video calls. So there are clear benefits, but companies really need to find ways to improve how people stay in touch.

results.structuredChinese: 我觉得学校只教考试内容肯定不够，因为学生以后还需要工作、沟通和合作。不过基础知识也不能丢，它是学习其他能力的底子。关键是平衡，例如设计得好的小组任务可以同时训练知识运用和团队协作，但如果只是少数人完成全部工作，就没有意义。
results.spokenEnglish: I don't think schools can get away with teaching to the test alone, because students are going to need so much more than that once they enter the workforce — things like communication and collaboration. That said, you can't just throw out the fundamentals either; they're the foundation everything else is built on. The real challenge is striking a balance. A well-designed group project, for instance, can get students applying what they've learned while also picking up teamwork skills. But the thing is, if it turns into one or two people doing all the work while everyone else coasts, the whole exercise becomes pretty pointless.

results.structuredChinese: 限制私家车可能缓解拥堵和污染，但公平性是个问题。市中心公共交通密集，限制开车比较可行；住在郊区的人可能没有可靠替代方式。政策能否奏效取决于公共交通覆盖、班次和具体限制方式，也需要平衡环境效益、通勤需求和不同收入群体承担的成本。
results.spokenEnglish: Restricting private cars might ease congestion and cut pollution, but fairness is the sticking point. In the city centre, where public transport is already dense, it's fairly workable. People in the suburbs, though, often don't have a reliable alternative. Whether the policy actually delivers comes down to three things: how extensive the public transport network is, how frequent the services are, and what form the restrictions take. You've also got to weigh environmental gains against commuting needs and the uneven costs different income groups would bear.
